gloss: lower seat, seat of lesser honor

definitions.gloss: lower seat, seat of lesser honor
definitions.explanation: The seat position farthest from the tokonoma (decorative alcove) or closest to the door in a traditional Japanese room. The seat taken by the person of lower status or the host. Opposite of {上座|かみざ}.

examples.japanese: ⟦{新人|しんじん}→新人：02500_shinjin⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{下座|げざ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{座|すわ}る→座る：00757_suwaru⟧。
examples.english: Newcomers sit in the lower seat.

examples.japanese: {下座|げざ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{入|い}り{口|ぐち}→入り口：02507_iriguchi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{近|ちか}い→近い：00530_chikai⟧⟦{席|せき}→席：02215_seki⟧だ。
examples.english: The lower seat is the one closest to the entrance.

examples.japanese: ⟦{上座|かみざ}→上座：11295_kamiza⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{下座|げざ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦マナー→マナー：11139_manaa⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{知|し}らない→知る：00458_shiru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦ビジネス→ビジネス：11162_bijinesu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{場|ば}→場：03699_ba⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{恥|はじ}→恥：12636_haji⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧かくこと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: If you don't know the etiquette of upper and lower seating, you may embarrass yourself in business settings.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
Seating hierarchy (⟦{上座|かみざ}→上座：11295_kamiza⟧/{下座|げざ}) is an important aspect of Japanese business and social etiquette. The rules apply in meeting rooms, taxis, elevators, and restaurants. Generally, the most senior person sits at ⟦{上座|かみざ}→上座：11295_kamiza⟧ (farthest from the door), while the most junior sits at {下座|げざ} (closest to the door).

FORMS:
{下|げ} (lower) + ⟦{座|ざ}→座：28170_za⟧ (seat)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {下座|げざ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{座|すわ}る→座る：00757_suwaru⟧: to sit in the lower seat
- ⟦{上座|かみざ}→上座：11295_kamiza⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{下座|げざ}: upper and lower seating positions
